There is this Fidelity Rewards Visa Signature Card. For those having any accounts with Fidelity Investments it’s pretty good. No annual fee. Pays straight 2% cash back for any purchase (I think they also have some kind of “points” program but those don’e seem to be very good). They also have some kind of sign up bonus I think.

The only catch is that you do have to have an account with Fidelity because this 2% rebate goes there. For millions of Fidelity customers this should present no problem. The money goes to that account automatically, at $25 minimum I think. Once in the account, you may choose to have it remain there or simply transfer to the external non-Fidelity account or withdraw.

Clean, simple, automatic and try to find many other cards giving 2% back. I recommend it. Have had it for 6-7 years now.

Wells Fargo is absolutely refusing to budge on approving me for the Business Platinum without some kind of documentation of the business. I applied as a sole prop using my legal name and not a dba, and straight from the California Secretary of State website you simply do NOT have to file anything unless you’re using a dba.

“A sole proprietorship is set up to allow an individual to own and operate a business. A sole proprietor has total control, receives all profits from and is responsible for taxes and liabilities of the business. If a sole proprietorship is formed with a name other than the individual’s name (example: John Smiths Fishing Shop), a Fictitious Business Name Statement must be filed with the county where the principal place of business is located.

“No formation documents are filed with the California Secretary of State’s office. Other state filings may be required depending on the type of business.”

https://www.sos.ca.gov/business-programs/business-entities/starting-business/types/#sole

A couple suggested edits:

– Both Navy Federal offers should be removed, because the offers expired and neither card has a sign-up bonus anymore.

– Avianca offers should probably be removed, because the offers were set to expire at the end of 2019. I haven’t been able to confirm whether the promo code actually stopped working, though.

– Hilton surpass might need to be removed or moved to the “YMMV” section. I’m seeing a 150,000 point offer, but no offer that includes the $100 statement credit.

– AmEx EveryDay should be removed or moved to “YMMV” section. Even with the incognito trick, I can only see a $10k offer (plus 0% intro APR and $0 balance transfer fee)

– Radisson offer should be removed, because the offer expired. Current offer is 85,000 points, which is not nearly as attractive.

– PenFed Pathfinder should be removed, because the card is no longer accepting applications.

– Consider adding the Capital One Venture, since 50,000 points for $3000 in spend and no AF is one of the best available offers right now. I understand that it used to be 75,000, but it seems unlikely to go back up to that level in the near future. If you don’t include it on the list, maybe put it on the “Not on List” section to be clear.

– Also consider the JetBlue Plus offer (40,000 TrueBlue points for $1000 in spend and $99 AF). It’s not the highest ever (they had a 60,000 point offer in 2017), but the net value by my valuations is competitive with the AmEx Green offer 45k offer and the Alaska 40k offer. It also has lower required spend than either of those offers.
